title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #205
gist: A link roundup marking one week in which hard tech absorbed enormous capital and hit real technical milestones: Terraform Industries produced >99.9% pure solar hydrogen at ~$2/kg, Base Power raised $1B at a $13B post, Hadrian $1.37B at $7.87B post and Valar Atomics $1B from Sequoia, Oklo took a reactor critical, OpenAI's internal 'Astra' model solved 10 open math/CS problems for under $2,000 of inference, and Tesla sited its 1-terawatt-of-compute 'Terafab' in Grimes County, Texas with an apparent free-electron-laser EUV source underneath. The author's implied through-line: atoms are re-rating, and Elon is now attacking ASML and TSMC simultaneously.

insights.claim: Terraform Industries sustained production of >99.9% pure hydrogen from a vertically integrated, California-manufactured electrolyzer stack coupled directly to a solar array at its Muroc desert test site, at a stated $2/kg.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Direct solar-coupled electrolysis at $2/kg without grid intermediation is the cost threshold that makes synthetic hydrocarbons plausible; watch it as a leading indicator for the green-hydrogen cost curve and for pressure on conventional refining economics.
insights.quote: the sustained production of >99.9% pure H2 from our vertically integrated, California-manufactured electrolyzer stack while it was coupled directly to a solar array at our Muroc desert test

insights.claim: The strategic prize in solar-to-hydrogen is not hydrogen itself but cheap synthetic hydrocarbons — effectively the ability to 'print refined oil' — which would decarbonize the large share of demand that batteries cannot serve.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Frames synthetic fuel as complementary to, not competing with, electrification — the addressable market is fuel-requiring end uses (aviation, heavy industry, chemicals) that battery TAM models exclude.
insights.quote: which would give humanity the power to basically print refined oil, make all sorts of things that require fuel, not just batteries, cheaper and cleaner
insights.locator: The gist is that Terraform is getting closer

insights.claim: Base Power Company raised $1B at a $13B post-money valuation and launched a product called Base Core.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A $13B mark on a distributed-power company sets a fresh private comp for the residential/grid-edge storage category and pulls valuation anchors up for peers.
insights.quote: Base Power Company Raises $1B at $13B Post, Launches Base Core
insights.locator: (2) Billion Dollar Rounds for Base Power

insights.claim: Hadrian raised $1.37B at a $7.87B post-money valuation, with CEO Chris Power arguing the world of atoms is 100x bigger than the world of bits.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Automated precision manufacturing is now funded at software-scale checks; watch for follow-on capital rotating into defense and aerospace supply-chain automation.
insights.quote: “We can’t forget the world of atoms is 100x bigger than the world of bits,” CEO Chris Power told NYSE.

insights.claim: Valar Atomics raised $1B in equity from Sequoia plus a reported $200B in debt, despite founder Isaiah having been told he could not start a nuclear company without a PhD in nuclear physics.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Debt of this scale attached to a startup reactor developer implies project-finance-style capital is now underwriting pre-revenue nuclear; the figure is extreme enough to warrant independent verification before use as a comp.
insights.quote: Valar Atomics Raises $1B from Sequoia & $200B in Debt

insights.claim: The author's implied view is that credentialism is a poor screen for hard-tech founders — Valar's founder was doubted 'the whole way' for lacking a nuclear physics PhD and kept proving doubters wrong.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: An underwriting heuristic: in regulated hard-tech categories, execution velocity may matter more than domain credentials, which is where mispriced founder risk sits.
insights.quote: you can’t start a nuclear company without a PhD in nuclear physics!
insights.locator: Valar is, sadly, not a not boring capital

insights.claim: The author discloses that Base Power and Hadrian are Not Boring portfolio companies while Valar Atomics is not, a conflict readers should weight when reading the enthusiasm.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Discount the framing on Base and Hadrian accordingly; the Valar praise carries no positional interest and is the cleaner signal.
insights.quote: Base is a not boring portfolio company and one of two companies (with Ramp) that I’ve written multiple Deep Dives on.

insights.claim: Oklo took a reactor critical for the first time, having submitted the first-ever custom combined license application for an advanced reactor in March 2020 for a ~1.5 MWe Aurora fast reactor at Idaho National Laboratory, and having initially been turned down for incompleteness.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: First criticality after a six-year NRC slog is the de-risking event advanced-nuclear equity has been waiting on; it also establishes a licensing precedent later entrants can follow faster.
insights.quote: submitting the first-ever custom combined license application for an advanced reactor in March 2020, for a ~1.5 MWe Aurora fast reactor at Idaho National Laboratory, before getting turned down for incompleteness

insights.claim: Oklo is differentiated from newer advanced reactor companies because it had to fight through the old NRC regulatory regime rather than a reformed one, implying later entrants face an easier path.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If the regulatory bottleneck has genuinely loosened, the scarcity premium on Oklo's licensing lead compresses over time even as the sector-wide opportunity widens.
insights.quote: Unlike a lot of the newfangled advanced reactor companies, Oklo had to fight through the old NRC regulatory regime to get here
insights.locator: Speaking of nuclear… I’m a simple man.

insights.claim: An internal version of Astra, OpenAI's next major model family, solved 10 major open problems in mathematics, quantum complexity, and theoretical computer science.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Frontier-model capability jumps in formal reasoning are the input that resets research-productivity assumptions; watch which scientific workflows get automated first.
insights.quote: An internal version of Astra, @OpenAI’s next major model family, solved 10 major open problems in mathematics, quantum complexity, and theoretical computer science.

insights.claim: Generating the proofs for all 10 breakthroughs combined cost under $2,000 at Sol API prices, per OpenAI's Noam Brown.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: The economics, not the capability, are the news: research-grade output at four-figure total inference cost means the binding constraint on scientific throughput shifts from compute spend to problem selection.
insights.quote: The cost of generating the proofs for all 10 of these breakthroughs combined was under $2,000 at Sol API prices.

insights.claim: The author is deliberately skeptical of the reaction to Astra, treating the 'we are in the Singularity and all the charts are up from here' framing as an overreaction even while conceding it might be right.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A useful sentiment marker: even reliably optimistic tech commentators are hedging on AGI-timeline updates, suggesting positioning based on capability headlines alone is crowded.
insights.quote: which has caused a lot of people to freak out and update their timelines and claim that we are in the Singularity and that all the charts are up from here, which… maybe!

insights.claim: Astra may ship publicly as soon as the following week and may be branded GPT-6 rather than another GPT-5.x point release, per AI leaker 'leo'.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A major-version rather than point release implies a pricing and capability step-change; watch for competitor response and API price resets within weeks of launch.
insights.quote: This may be GPT-6 instead of another GPT-5.x. So prepare yourself.
insights.locator: The fun thing is, you might get to play

themes.theme: Terafab: Musk attacks ASML and TSMC at once

insights.claim: Tesla sited Terafab — described as the largest chip manufacturing facility ever, targeting over 1 terawatt of compute per year — in Grimes County, Texas, with Tesla and SpaceX investing $16.8 billion for the initial buildout.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A $16.8B first-phase captive fab is a direct demand signal for semicap equipment and Texas power, and a long-term supply threat to merchant foundry pricing.
insights.quote: the largest chip manufacturing facility ever, with the goal of producing over 1 terawatt of compute per year

insights.claim: Terafab appears to include a particle accelerator beneath the facility generating short-wavelength photons for lithography — a free-electron-laser-based EUV source that Elon Musk endorsed with 'FEL FTW' when Extropic's Beff Jezos flagged it.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: An in-house FEL EUV source would bypass the single-supplier bottleneck in advanced lithography; even a credible attempt pressures the assumption that EUV access is permanently gated.
insights.quote: Elon replied, “FEL FTW.”
insights.locator: The coolest part of this is a detail

insights.claim: One synchrotron could feed several EUV scanners at once with ultra-bright, clean light — 'way more photons and less mess than today's tin-plasma sources' — per Phil Beisel.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: The economic argument for FEL EUV is amortizing one light source across many scanners; if it works, per-wafer lithography cost structure and the ASML tool-pricing model both change.
insights.quote: with way more photons and less mess than today’s tin-plasma sources

insights.claim: The author's headline read on Terafab is that Elon Musk is going after ASML and TSMC simultaneously by building a particle accelerator — vertical integration extended all the way down to the photon source.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A concrete, if long-dated, bear thesis vector for both ASML's tool monopoly and TSMC's foundry share; near-term the risk is narrative, not volume.
insights.quote: All of which means that Elon seems to be going after ASML and TSMC at the same time by building a particle accelerator. Now that’s vertical integration.

insights.claim: The author attributes Terafab's Texas siting partly to California political hostility, noting the $16.8 billion 'might have spent in California if former State Assemblywoman Lorena Gonzalez hadn't told Elon to go f*ck himself a few years back.'
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Reinforces the capital-migration trade: Texas capturing megaprojects means state-level industrial policy and permitting posture are now material inputs to siting forecasts and regional power demand.
insights.quote: money it might have spent in California if former State Assemblywoman Lorena Gonzalez hadn’t told Elon to go f*ck himself a few years back

themes.theme: What the roundup signals about the cycle

insights.claim: In a single week the roundup logs roughly $3.4B of announced equity into three hard-tech companies (Base $1B, Hadrian $1.37B, Valar $1B) plus a $16.8B industrial commitment, indicating capital is rotating decisively toward atoms-based businesses.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Private hard-tech marks are being set at software-like multiples; the follow-through to watch is whether public-market comps in energy, nuclear, and industrial automation re-rate to match.
insights.locator: (2) Billion Dollar Rounds for Base Power

insights.claim: Nuclear appears twice in one week from opposite directions — a $1B Sequoia-backed startup raise and an incumbent-path first criticality — suggesting the sector's bottleneck has shifted from regulatory permission to manufacturing throughput.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If the constraint is now factories rather than licenses, the value migrates to reactor manufacturing capacity and supply chain rather than to permit holders.
insights.quote: Valar is going to pump out so many nuclear reactors.
insights.locator: Valar is, sadly, not a not boring capital

insights.claim: The post is explicitly abbreviated because the author spent the day at his daughter's birthday, and the majority of items — including cancer-fighting psychedelics, vertiports, Ribbit's power letter, a Leopold post-mortem, Extropic, Jeff Dean, and Atoms x Joby — sit behind a paywall in the Extra Doses section.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: The free portion is a partial sample; the named-but-unelaborated items (Ribbit power letter, Leopold post-mortem, Atoms x Joby) are leads worth sourcing elsewhere rather than treating as covered.
insights.quote: Extra Doses: Science Breakthroughs, Ribbit Power Letter, Leopold Post-Mortem, Extropic, Jeff Dean, Atoms x Joby
